failure_definition: Cases exhibiting highest anatomical reconstruction discrepancy (top outlier ASSD and HD95)

anatomical_failure_drivers: Restricted/small lung volume causing relative boundary overestimation
Hyperinflated lung volume exceeding common PCA deformation modes
Restricted/small lung volume causing relative boundary overestimation
Shallow AP thoracic depth (138.8 mm) inducing lateral view projection compression
Restricted/small lung volume causing relative boundary overestimation
Shallow AP thoracic depth (154.1 mm) inducing lateral view projection compression

systemic_failure_mechanisms.description: Patients with high diaphragmatic domes or blunted posterior costophrenic angles show local Hausdorff discrepancies exceeding 12 mm due to projection overlap with abdominal organs on frontal CXR.

Patients with pectus excavatum or narrow anteroposterior thoracic dimensions (<170 mm) suffer from lateral projection occlusion where anterior mediastinal structures compress the projected lung boundary.

When unilateral pathology, atelectasis, or surgical resection alters the canonical 1.22 right-to-left lung ratio, symmetric PCA coupling forces partial volume compensation onto the contralateral lung.

mitigation_recommendations: Incorporate dedicated diaphragmatic boundary loss in Phase 6 training
Expose calibrated simultaneous confidence bands in the clinical viewer to visually highlight high-uncertainty basilar regions
Require clinical alert when bilateral asymmetry ratio exceeds [1.05, 1.40]
